quest.title: The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc
quest.description: You encounter a strange Nochtlin on the hill beside Wavey Bay...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Primogem x50, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.text: The crisis emerges, yet the tribal leaders bicker endlessly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi there! What are you doing here...
Let Tenoyollotzin bring his "talking stick" over, and let it mediate the discussion...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, Teno-who?
Tenoyollotzin belongs no longer to any tribe, yet his fury still burns, unquenched.
When he set foot on the path of fate, the first to come forward and receive him was the great runner, Wanjiru.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wanjiru? What are you talking about?
Wanjiru!
...This was a moment that left no trace in the annals of history! At the very instant those two met, Wanjiru bolted without so much as a backward glance — as if startled by some unseen force!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhm... What's going on? Who's he talking to?
Tenoyollotzin's suspicions surged as he glanced around, and he spotted a snaggletoothed child lurking by the side of the road. The child had been the one to scare off poor Wanjiru...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A snaggletoothed child? Hey, Paimon'll have you know...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Her teeth are in perfect condition!
The insolent child provoked Wanjiru, and even went so far as to bare her teeth... an act of utmost sacrilege. Tenoyollotzin was filled with rage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! P—Paimon's sorry if she disturbed you! Please don't be filled with rage!

dialogues.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
dialogues.text: With but a single word, the valorous veteran frightened the churlish child nearly to tears. Yet every warrior knows this truth... To forgive the enemy with flowers is to loose an arrow into one's own heart.

dialogues.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
dialogues.text: And so the last survivor of Tenochtzitoc raised his club, brandished it at the rocks and prickly pears, and declared, "Let my stick talk bloody sense into this brat! For Wanjiru!"

choices.text: Looks like you're all talk, and no stick...

response.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
response.text: Ohohoha, a golden-haired child appeared! Tenoyollotzin's very words were the club he used to fell his foes!

choices.text: There will be no felling of any Paimons unless you get past me.

response.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
response.text: #Ohohoha, a golden-haired child appeared! Tenoyollotzin would teach {M#him}{F#her} the might of the heavens and the earth...!

choices.text: Can you please calm down, and we'll be on our way...

response.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
response.text: Their feeble repentance came far too late! They would be made to pay for their recklessness!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: We're good friends, Papar — our mothers are good friends too. We promised to build this resort together... How am I supposed to face them with you like this...?

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: If your mother gets ticked off, she'll get my mother ticked off, and then I'll be in the firing line — if that happens, you better believe I'm gonna make it your problem as well!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: So, for the sake of our mothers, could you at least answer me, and let me know you're listening?

dialogues.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
dialogues.text: As Tenoyollotzin gazed upon the vast burning plains, a turbid black tide welled up on the horizon.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Alright, I guess I should tell you how our fathers are faring...

dialogues.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
dialogues.text: Hold on!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Eh? You're awake!?

dialogues.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
dialogues.text: ...It's that old lady...

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Papar, what is it? What old lady?

dialogues.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
dialogues.text: Silence! Hold them off outside!

dialogues.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
dialogues.text: If you get any closer, the next time you'll be seeing our mothers is from the inside of a coffin!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Master Pucli, we're here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what's going on? You look terrified...

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Papar... He's awake, and he called my mother an old hag— There's something wrong. His illness has gotten worse!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? We'd better go check on him!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So this is that out-of-sorts employee?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey, you! Clothes off!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A—Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: He's definitely not one of the resort staff...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Last chance. Get rid of that disguise, or I'll make you wish you did!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hold on, something's not right...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Citlali steps forward and tears away the costume, but there is nobody inside. All she's left with is a Nochtli costume with traces of lingering warmth.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Are you kidding me? He got away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's going on? Was "Tenoyollotzin" hollow on the inside!?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: No, there was someone in this costume, alright, but it looks like they slipped away just before we got here.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ah, darn it! It must have been Enjou. I can sense the aura of my mark on him...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so the "Tenoyollotzin" we met just now was Enjou in disguise? How long has he been playing us along!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Probably since the very beginning...

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Wait... If that's not Papar, then where's Papar!? Oh, Archons, I deserve the scolding our mothers are going to give me...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we'll get to the bottom of this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aaagh! I can't believe Enjou tricked us again! We have to catch him!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, it seems he fled in a hurry. My arrival probably threw him off, which means he might have abandoned some things around the camp...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then let's get searching for clues!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: ...Tch, that old hag! She's even more of a nuisance than I am...

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Guess I'll just have to wait and see how things pan out...

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop fighting!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: I'm terribly sorry. I'm Pucli, the entertainment supervisor at the resort... But that can wait. No one's hurt, are they?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}!? Where'd you get hit? Paimon'll go find a doctor...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm just messing around.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph! You're going to give Paimon a heart attack! Don't joke about serious stuff like that!

response.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
response.text: Argh... Tenoyollotzin was wounded in both body and heart. The joyous battle had been halted, leaving him unfulfilled...

response.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
response.text: Like a brief storm, a faint thunderclap, half a hiss of flames, a thin pall of smoke...

response.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
response.text: The last survivor of Tenochtzitoc swung his stone club with fury, rending heaven and shattering earth, the volcano in his heart about to erupt...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Did he hit himself on the head with his own club or something? If anyone's going to erupt here, it should be us!

response.speaker: Pucli
response.text: *sigh* It's... a very long story. I need to take him back to his hut to rest. I'll explain everything later.

response.speaker: Pucli
response.text: The hut's not far from here. We can meet back up there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And quite right too! He deserves it for attacking us out of nowhere like that...

talks.objective: Head to the hut and talk to Pucli

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's gone all quiet... What's up with him?

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: I'm sorry for the inconvenience, dear guests. His name is Papar, and he's one of our on-site actors.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: On-site actors?

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: They're quite common in theme parks nowadays — members of staff who role-play as characters and interact with the visitors.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh! So you're saying this guy was... just acting?

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Yes, but also no... Urgh, please allow me to explain.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: We've stationed actors around the themed resort to enhance the immersive experience for our guests. These actors are in character as members of the tribe that once lived here — the Tenochtzitoc.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: There was once a great hero from this tribe, known to all of Natlan, who was named Tenoch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tenoch! So this was his home!? Then "Tenoyollotzin" is...

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: "Tenoyollotzin" was a respectful title given to Tenoch. It means "the honored heart of Tenochtzitoc."

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: The idea was for Papar to perform in encounters with other heroes, and even to allow guests to test their own martial prowess...

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Lately, though, something's gotten into him. He's been acting erratically, and nobody can get through to him. You've seen it yourselves... It's like he's reciting a script.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What script!? It's more like he's writing himself into every scene!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: In any case, please accept my sincerest apologies for this mess. We'll have to suspend this attraction until the matter is resolved.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Please come back with me, dear guests. We'll make sure to properly compensate you for the trouble caused...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And what about this "Tenoyollotzin" fellow?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! If he runs into some other tourists, they might not get off so easily...

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: You're right, but please don't worry. I'll make sure to take care of everything.

dialogues.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
dialogues.text: A tragedy most heartbreaking! The lonesome Tenoyollotzin had yet to fulfill his duty, but now he was beset by baffling, cacophonous interlopers...

dialogues.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
dialogues.text: He could no longer bear witness to such a ridiculous sight, so he pushed aside the three fools who blocked his way and continued onwards, stone club across his shoulder, to traverse the treacherous unknowns ahead...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You don't even have a stone club! Wait, he's getting away!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Not if I can help it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Pucli takes out a peculiar blowpipe and takes aim at the fleeing figure...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: *Thwip* His aim is true and "Tenoyollotzin" is struck!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: *Thump* The hero sways gently for a moment and then collapses to the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! A sneak attack!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Sorry, Papar, but it's time for you to take a nap. I promise we'll find a way to get you better...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Have you asked a doctor to check him out? Maybe he's just gone a little... uhm... loopy?

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Of course I looked for him — I've chased him from Easybreeze Market to Wavey Bay!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He sure seems dangerous... Oh, right!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He was blabbing about "Wanjiru" just now. Do you think this might have something to do with the story of the six heroes of Natlan?

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Surely that was just another memorized line, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But he sounded like he was talking to someone.

dialogues.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
dialogues.text: Wanjiru!

dialogues.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
dialogues.text: ...This was a moment that left no trace in the annals of history! At the very instant those two met, Wanjiru bolted without so much as a backward glance — as if startled by some unseen force!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's like there was an invisible actor there... or something. And he said Paimon scared them off!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Invisible? Well, I have heard some rumors about hidden spirits lurking around these parts...

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Maybe Papar's gotten himself mixed up in something dangerous. I should find a shaman to help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't that perfect? There should be plenty of tourists from the Masters of the Night-Wind at the resort.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: As it happens, a young shaman did check into the resort this morning... But it doesn't feel right to bother guests with this sort of thing...

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: In any case, I'll investigate the rumors regarding the hidden spirits first before deciding what to do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Since you've got no other leads, why not let us help out? You go dig around for those rumors, and we'll help you look for the shaman!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: That's much too kind of you! I wouldn't know how to make it up to two guests if they were to spend their vacation on something like this...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It wouldn't be a very relaxing vacation if we left this problem unresolved.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! If we wait around, things might get worse! And we've got lots of friends at the resort... It'd be bad if they ran into that Tenoyollotzin guy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, hey, we'd be more than happy to help! Point us in the direction of the shaman, and we'll bring him over in a jiffy!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Okay then... You have my sincerest gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: The shaman arrived this morning, and I'm told he's an up-and-coming hotshot in the Masters of the Night-Wind. I'm guessing he's probably wandering around the hill in the northernmost part of Wavey Bay.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then that's where we're headed! We'll be right back!

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Hello, you two. Is something the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: #Huh!? The great hero {NICKNAME} and Paimon! How fortunate I am to cross paths with you here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You look familiar! Have we met before?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Have you forgotten? I'm Leyla, that spirit-duffer! You, Master Ororon, and the great shaman Citlali once saved my life!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Leyla recounts an event that happened not too long ago, when you helped a member of the Masters of the Night-Wind return his lost spirit to his body.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you! Well, you're looking healthy, Leyla! Paimon almost didn't recognize you with your hat on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...But, uh... Did you say "Master" Ororon?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Yes, I did! I'm currently studying the mystic arts under Master Ororon's tutelage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aaand... does Ororon know about this?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Well! It's something of a... "one-sided teaching relationship."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So he doesn't even know he's your teacher!? What kind of a student are you, then?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: As someone who used to be a spirit-duffer, if Citlali hadn't saved me and Ororon hadn't taught me... There's no way I could have ever become a shaman.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: If a teacher is like a gardener, I'd gladly be one of their carrots — and let them water me with knowledge!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you really think we can rely on this guy?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Come again? I couldn't hear that very well...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... Paimon was just saying how nice it is to run into an old friend!

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Master often calls me "friend" as well, but I won't have it. Master is Master, and Master's Granny is Master Granny. That's just how things are.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: #As for you, most venerable {NICKNAME}, I know that you are friends with the great shaman Citlali... Which makes you my Master {M#Gramps}{F#Granny} too!

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: I'm afraid it would be discourteous of me to address you simply as "friend."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds to Paimon like you picked up a lot more than just mystic arts from Ororon...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay... let's get back to business.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! We're actually here to ask for your help, Leyla!

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Help? From me? Rest assured, good masters, whatever task you entrust to me, I shall fulfill it to the best of my abilities!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain to Leyla what happened earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: I see... So, you think he's being possessed?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's right. What's your take on the situation?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: The Easybreeze Holiday Resort is indeed a location with vibrant spiritual energies, I could sense that as soon as I arrived. So it wouldn't be amiss to assume that some invisible entity could have been involved...

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Can you take me to that spot with the swing you mentioned earlier? I'd like to confirm a few things.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure thing, Leyla! We'll show you the way!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is the spot!

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Hmm... Just as I thought...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: I truly was held back by apical dominance...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Apica-what now?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: It's a botanical phenomenon.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: The stems of some vegetables grow incredibly quickly and absorb a large amount of nutrients, impeding the growth of lateral buds and leaves. If you want to encourage more foliage, you have to remove the apical bud at the top of the stem.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Master Ororon said that I was once held back by my spirit-duffer problem. That is, until I found a way to clip it off the top...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And then?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: And then I blossomed into a healthy vegetable with lush and verdant foliage.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Teyvat to Leyla, you do remember why we're here, right?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Of course! It might sound like I'm going off topic, but I was just trying to say that I've discovered some traces of spiritual energy.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: They're weak and very, very faint. An ordinary shaman might have walked right by without noticing a thing.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: But I'm no ordinary shaman anymore! Thanks to Master Ororon... I've grown into a plant to be proud of!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Leyla! Can you please drop the vegetable metaphors and focus on the matter at hand!? You'll have plenty of time to think about stems and buds AFTER we solve this mystery!

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: #A—Ahh! Yes, uhm... Of course! Just as Master {M#Gramps}{F#Granny} said, the afflicted actor conversed with some kind of presence here.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: I'm going to use my clairvoyance and try to follow these faint traces of spiritual energy. It might be possible to glimpse the presence's true form.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: But first, I need to prepare something very important...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhm... What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: There we go!

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: #What sharp eyes you have, Master {M#Gramps}{F#Granny}! These are indeed carrots, and this is a carrot ring, but they're not for eating.

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: This is a medium of divination that will help with clairvoyance.

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: In my tribe, everyone has their own unique method of divination. Some use graffiti, others use smoke or water... I use vegetables.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that's novel... but does it actually work?

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Master once told me, "Do not underestimate the humble vegetable — it is the eyes and ears of the earth. Born of the soil, gifted with its spirit and blood, it bears the symbols and memories of the land."

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Every time you eat vegetables, it's like suckling at the teat of Mother Teyvat... sharing in the histories and mysteries passed down through generations.

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: That's why we eat vegetables and not grass or leaves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh! Paimon's never eating another vegetable as long as she lives! She'd rather eat Slimes!

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: That's a pity, Paimon. You could have a chance to grow your wisdom.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Please just continue with whatever you're doing, Leyla. Paimon won't say anything ever again...

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Feel free to speak your mind, Master Paimon! Thank you for allowing me to share my knowledge with you both.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can you please just start already!?

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: #Of course! Here, Paimon, and you too, Master {M#Gramps}{F#Granny}.

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Put your hands on my shoulders. It will help you see...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhm... Is this safe?

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: I've gleaned from the spiritual traces that the hidden presence is neither powerful nor violent. So yes, I think it's quite safe.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm ready!

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Alright, let's get started...

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Carrot ring, o carrot ring — make visible these unseen things!

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Show me, show me, where is their grave?

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Carrot ring, o carrot ring — make visible these unseen things!

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Show me, show me, where did they fall?

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Please allow me to see...

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: How did things turn out this way... Oh, man, my head hurts...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you okay, Leyla?

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: I'm fine! But I'm afraid I've reached my limit. Did you see that? Truly remarkable, I dare say...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It was like a dream...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What did it all mean?

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: All I know is that the Asha on the swing is probably the spirit you're looking for. Although I'm not sure how it gained the ability to hide itself...

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Moreover, the spiritual energy traces belong to more than just one Asha, which lines up with what we saw. There must be several of them nearby.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are they the cause of the problem?

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: It's hard to say. But it's likely that actor started to lose control of himself because he was affected in some way by the Asha's departure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we can track down those Asha, we should at least be able to calm him down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's how it is... Vegetables aside, it looks like you've learned some real skills, Leyla!

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: I have to work hard not to tarnish Master's good name!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What about the ones we saw later on?

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: I, too, am more concerned about what we saw afterwards... The fabric those Asha were gathered around — it looked a lot like the woven scrolls we use in the Masters of the Night-Wind.

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: And that mysterious place that appeared later, along with the strange figure standing in the carrot ring... It all felt very familiar somehow, but I'm not sure why...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's okay, we can think about that stuff later. For now, we have leads that could help that "Tenoyollotzin" guy!

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: #Right... But, uh, Paimon, Master {M#Gramps}{F#Granny}... I think I'll excuse myself from that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Why?

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: The truth is... I feel a little uneasy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Didn't you just say you've grown into a vegetable Ororon could be proud of!?

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Indeed... But even the carrots are whispering warnings, "When the field is filled with crops, frost will come to claim them."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That sounds serious...

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: The great shaman Citlali instructed me to come to Tenochtzitoc to relax... but she also told me to let her know if things started to get strange.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Citlali sent you here? Aren't you on vacation?

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Whether this is a vacation or not depends entirely on the whims of the aforementioned "frost." Right now, all I want to do is rush back to Master's greenhouse...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, you're starting to make Paimon feel nervous now...

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Fear not, Paimon! The tallest vegetables are always the first to fall to frost — you should be safe for a while.

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Oh, and speaking of vegetables, you can keep these carrots. Now that the divination's over, they've turned into spirit mediums for the Asha.

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Just sprinkle some of their juice into your eyes, and you'll be able to see the invisible Asha. That should help you track them down.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thanks, Leyla.

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: #I should be the one thanking you! It's an honor to be able to help you out, Master {M#Gramps}{F#Granny}. I'll be going now, so take care, and good luck in your search!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...And there he goes. Do you think he was overreacting?

choices.text: Overreacting or not, let's watch our step.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay! Let's go back to the hut first and check on our guy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon hopes what we learned about the Asha will come in handy!

choices.text: No need to worry — if things go wrong, there are plenty of vegetables taller than us in this garden.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon feels a little better hearing you say that. Let's go back to the hut and check on our guy.

choices.text: We can eat once we've finished our work.

response.speaker: Leyla
response.text: Even once we've finished, these are not for eating...

dialogues.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
dialogues.text: The second to come forward and embrace Tenoyollotzin was the brave Menilek...

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: That's right. The third was the cunning Sanhaj Kompore, the fourth was the young Burkina, and the fifth was Sundjatta...

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Papar, what do you want to do? You can't go looking for them now, they've been gone for hundreds of years...

dialogues.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
dialogues.text: The sixth to go with Tenoyollotzin was the nemesis from his youth, the giant Tupac...

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: How am I supposed to explain to your mother how you ended up like this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! He's awake!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: You're back! Don't worry, he's just reciting lines again. The witch doctor's sedatives are very effective. His erratic behavior earlier was probably due to something agitating him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's a relief! Anyway, Pucli, we found the shaman, and he told us what to do.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Pucli what happened with Leyla.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: So it was all because of the Asha... Well, that's a surprise, but knowing that should make things easier.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Easier? How? The resort's huge, how are we supposed to track down a bunch of invisible Asha?

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: I'll handle that. I'll get my staff to investigate supernatural occurrences around the resort — things like empty swings moving on their own. That way, we might just find our invisible Asha.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like a plan!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Given our lack of knowledge on the Asha, this is our only choice right now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, those Asha are really strange... They look like Monetoo, but their colors are way more vibrant, and they seem to be smarter!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: That's one way of looking at it, but it might be more helpful to think of them as having a soul.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: In Tenochtzitoc culture, the word "Asha" has two meanings, one of which roughly translates to "benevolent soul."

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Many believe that Asha are Monetoo with a soul, and that's why they're smarter and more approachable.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh, Paimon gets it! So what's the other meaning? Hehe, Paimon bets it's got something to do with the spirit of summertime that embodies this resort!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's not a bad guess, but the second meaning is actually something closer to "ashes."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ashes?

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Yes, ashes blown over from the Mare Jivari.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So the Asha are connected to the Mare Jivari?

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: You may not know this, but there's a vast tract of land to the West of Tenochtzitoc that was once the Mare Jivari. It is a place of sorrow born from the Abyssal invasion.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Warriors were reduced to dust, their souls imprisoned and bound to the land. That is, until the whole Mare Jivari mysteriously vanished about twenty years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: It was around that time that the Asha first appeared. Naturally, people made the connection to the Mare Jivari.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder they're so willing to approach the people of Natlan. They're all caught up in the legend of the Mare Jivari...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}! Paimon just thought of something. When Leyla showed us that strange place just now, it looked like the place we went to search for Bennett before! You don't think...

response.speaker: Pucli
response.text: Ah, there I go, getting sidetracked. I'm going to focus on Papar first. Give me a day, and I'll round up all the locations where the invisible Asha might show up.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What are you going to do about him?

response.speaker: Pucli
response.text: I plan to let him stay here for now. He might get unnecessarily stimulated if he leaves this familiar environment.

response.speaker: Pucli
response.text: The resort has also designated this a restricted area, so rest assured that no tourists will accidentally come wandering by.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's good... Papar attacked us, but we won't hold it against him. We'll find a way to cure him for sure!

response.speaker: "Tenoyollotzin"
response.text: And so, Tenoyollotzin gathered allies from the six great tribes. Glittering like the flames of roaring wildfire, they crashed into the mountains of darkness...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Stay strong, Papar! Even in your imaginary quest to be a hero...!

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: It was just a sedative, Papar. You're alright, don't worry.

talks.objective: Head to the reception to look for Pucli

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Ah, you're both here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Pucli! Any news?

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Surprisingly, no. Although I did come across some suspicious information.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: It dates back to when we were planning the construction of Easybreeze Holiday Resort. Workers near the "Tenoyollotzin" huts often complained that their materials had gone missing.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: The missing materials were soon found in the wilderness nearby, but no one ever admitted to moving them.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: There were also rumors of workers being frightened by water rippling when there was no wind, or wild beasts being spooked for unknown reasons... all around the same area.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that sounds just like the work of invisible Asha. But why'd they only show up in one area?

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: I also found it strange. Maybe there's something special near the huts?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like we'd better conduct some fieldwork.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: Let me mark the location on your map. In the meantime, I'll head to the huts to check on my staff.

talks.objective: Prepare to search for invisible Asha

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: According to Pucli, the hidden Asha should be somewhere around here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess that means it's time to use Leyla's magic carrots, right? Let's give it a try!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You squeeze some juice out of the carrots and gently apply it to both your eyes and Paimon's.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...That smells fresh and yummy, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look! There's an Asha, right there! On the lake! Whoa, Paimon can't believe those carrots actually worked!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Are you ready?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure! Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's a little worried about this one... but okay, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You place Sanhaj's relic on the stone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Look! The seat in the center... It's glowing! {NICKNAME}... Do you wanna try sitting on it?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Paimon! Where are you?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #({NICKNAME} disappeared after {M#he}{F#she} sat on the pedestal. Did {M#he}{F#she} get transported somewhere else? Ugh, it's too dangerous, I've got to follow {M#him}{F#her}...)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (Wait, no way! I'm the only one who knows what's happened, I can't just rush in after them. The Tzitzimitl can't stray too far from me, either... If we all get trapped inside, we're dead meat...)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #(But I can't just walk away! That Abyss Order rat could show up at any moment... I can't let him threaten {NICKNAME} and Paimon.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (...This is bad. I have to find a way to inform Mavuika, or at least leave a message that can be passed on to her...)
Oh my, oh my, I'm sorry to be a bother, but may I ask if this is the Hotel of the Sacred Flame? What stylish chairs it has.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...When it rains, it pours.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Oh my, oh my, could it be? The fearsome Granny Itztli, the one who's been chasing me everywhere... When did you get into the customer service industry?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Abyssal rat! Still running that rodent mouth of yours! Is this another one of your schemes?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: I admit that I can be somewhat loquacious, and I adore a good scheme as much as the next "Abyssal rat"... but this is my first time visiting this tawdry establishment.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: I thought I'd be able to reach the Mare Jivari through that woven scroll — who would've thought it would take me here? I guess this is what people mean when they say "it's a small world"?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Oh my! I must be disturbing you during your shift, Granny Itztli. I shall take my leave.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: See yourself out.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: My! You're really letting a perfectly good customer go? Won't this look bad for your key performance indicators?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Granny doesn't have the time to entertain you right now, so please get your sorry hind out of my sight.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: #Of course, of course... I don't suppose this has anything to do with {NICKNAME}'s mysterious absence? We're old friends, you know, me and {M#him}{F#her}. I just thought I should say hello, seeing as I'm here...

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: #...Or perhaps I could draw your attention to {M#his}{F#her} familiar scent left behind on that chair over there? Might I investigate?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Wow, scent? Guess I was wrong about you. Rather than a rat, you appear to be {NICKNAME}'s Abyssal mutt.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Why, I am most offended... Such vitriol... From the mouth of a dear old lady, no less!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #You mistake me — I'm just so touched that a little lost dog would travel a thousand miles to reunite with its {M#master}{F#mistress}... It's enough to move Granny to tears.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well then, Itzpapa, let the mangy dog perform his trick.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well? You have been taught how to sit, surely? Or do you need a treat to coax it out of you?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: ...I must admit, as a representative of the Abyss Order, I am... slightly perturbed by your sudden change in attitude, Granny.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So not a dog, but a scaredy-cat instead? The Abyss Order can't possibly be full of cowards like you — no wonder they're stuck wallowing in mediocrity.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Think not of my incompetence as something all my colleagues possess. I am, as you first said, merely a rat subject to the mockeries of others. Being cautious is how a rat survives, no?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: So, just to be sure that I'm not about to walk into a trap, how about we make a deal, Granny?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Papar, the employee who was role-playing a hero, is currently safe. Might I exchange him for safe passage to the Mare Jivari?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: As long as I can reach the Mare unhindered, I can guarantee that Papar will return to his friend, and all will be well. What do you think, dear Granny?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...And what exactly do you want to do in the Mare Jivari?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: The elderly should know better than to hover over the shoulders of the youth, prying into all their personal secrets.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmph... Such flowery speech, it's a pity I can't be bothered to commit it to memory. However, you'd do best to remember every word I'm about to say.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: That seems a little unfair...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Isn't it the duty of a grandson to listen to their Granny? Keep those ears peeled, lest I peel them off your head.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The throne behind me leads to a place none of us knows about. If you want to go there, you'd best become as compliant as a docile capybara.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #No vandalism, no hurting the flora, find {NICKNAME} and Paimon, and ensure their safety.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: #Understood. I swear on {NICKNAME}'s name to do as you say.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You young people are always so keen on swearing oaths. As for an old-timer like me, I prefer a safer approach. I just need you to cooperate for a moment...

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: What do you mean by cooperate?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hush, hush, my ratty little grandson. This won't take long...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Itzpapa, hold him down!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Do you remember that time we helped Leyla get his spirit back? The whole time he was being tricked by that "Kokuchuu" guy.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: If I'm not mistaken, it was he that Leyla saw during his ritual.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So, I looked into this guy and found out he once escaped from Kinich while using the name "Sanka"... It turns out he's one slippery rat.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Kinich even told me you've crossed paths with him before...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've crossed paths... Wait, there's no way... I—It's Enjou!?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: "Enjou"? Is that his real name...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It could be another alias.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whatever he's called, he's a clerk who works for the Abyss Order. He's great at lying and great at slipping away... Are you here to catch him, Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So he's an Abyss Order goon. Well, we can't let him get away now, can we?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (That rat! He should know you don't mess with an old lady's pride, yet that lousy fiend took me for a fool! Just you wait, Granny Itztli's going to make you regret the day you were born!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm... Hey, Citlali! Is everything okay? You're making a really scary face...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmph, do you still have the stuff I left with you last time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Stuff? Uhm, {NICKNAME}, maybe we should take a look...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Take out Sanhaj's relic)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright, it's still in good condition. Now the other one.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Take out the map)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well, that's a relief. I was worried Enjou might have swiped them from you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! That great big liar wouldn't dare show his face around us!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Anyway, be careful. He's lurking somewhere nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He is!? How can you be so sure?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hehe... He may have gotten away from us last time, but I made sure to leave a mark on him. That way, I can track the rat no matter what hole he decides to crawl into. As long as he's nearby, I'll be able to sense him.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I had a vague sense of where he was from the moment I set foot in the resort. I never expected to bump into you two while tracking him, though.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you're saying he's nearby?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yes. Unfortunately, the mark only gives me a rough guide to where he is... otherwise, I'd have caught him already.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #We should work together, {NICKNAME}. I get a sense that Enjou might have something to do with that employee's strange behavior.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awesome! With Citlali here, there's nothing to fear!

talks.objective: Head to the hut with Citlali
Search the area around the hut for clues

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now that we've read all three reports, what should we do next?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go to the place marked on the map.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Good idea! It looks like we're pretty close. We just have to figure out what the Abyss Order is up to!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Let's head out!

talks.objective: Head to the location marked on the map

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm... Wait a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright. We'll set out as soon as you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's a little worried about this one... but okay, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where in the world are we...?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I was unaware that such a place exists in Natlan...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Paimon can't believe even Citlali doesn't know where we are!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Blast! My connection to the Wayob's been severed...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What does that mean!?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It means we're probably not in Natlan anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? How? We were in the resort just a few seconds ago!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'd explain it if I could. Even though I can't sense the Wayob anymore, I can still sense the Night Kingdom's presence... This doesn't make sense...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's look around. Maybe we'll find some answers.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Better than standing around and gawking. Let's move, but be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's weird... There should be a weapon here, right?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: There are words carved on the back of this stone... Hmm, it belonged to Sanhaj.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This was Sanhaj's weapon? Where did it go... Ah! Could it be...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The relic?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's put it there and see if it does anything!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where the heck are we? We just touched that stone thing, and *fwoosh* now we're here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Aaand Citlali's nowhere to be seen.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This place looks like the Night Kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali said she could sense the Night Kingdom's presence just now. Maybe this is why?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why are there traces of the Abyss here? Didn't we get rid of them already?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe this isn't Natlan at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks like Natlan, but it's not Natlan... It looks like the Night Kingdom, but there's no Wayob connection, and the Abyss is still around... Waaah! Paimon's getting scared!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I just thought of something!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sanhaj once cast a border spell.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh!? Are you talking about that mini-Night Kingdom he summoned... Wouldn't that mean the Mare Jivari is right in front of us!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We won't know unless we look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then let's be careful!
#<color=#E1A4D0>{NICKNAME}, Paimon!</color>

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Someone's calling for us... It sounds like Citlali!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: <color=#E1A4D0>I've found you at last...</color>

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: En—En—Enjou!?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: <color=#E1A4D0>It's me, Citlali.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali!?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: #Ahem... Well, long time no see, {NICKNAME} and Paimon! I have to admit, this isn't what I thought our reunion would look like...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's gone back to being Enjou again!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Hearing the voice of that old hag come out of my youthful mouth is beyond mortifying...

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: <color=#E1A4D0>Shut up before I make you!</color>

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you okay, Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: <color=#E1A4D0>I'm fine. My body's back in the main hall, but I used a spell to attach a part of my spirit to this fool's body — this way, I can put him to good use.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Citlali's amazing, Paimon can't believe she can actually control Enjou's body!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Don't let her fool you — she's not that powerful! I'm only letting her do this because I cut a deal with her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A deal? So you sold your own body?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: In a partial, temporary, and limited transaction.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: <color=#E1A4D0>One that allows me to ensure your safety and keep him from threatening us. Anyway, I'm glad you're safe, both of you.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: <color=#E1A4D0>Here, this is Sanhaj's ritual sword, the Calamity of Eshu. I borrowed it from the chief before I set off from the Masters of the Night-Wind.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: <color=#E1A4D0>Since we don't know much about this area you're in, it's probably best to keep it close at hand, just in case.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, so this is what he used to summon the Night Kingdom?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: What a rare and precious treasure... I don't suppose it'd be a problem if I just... touched it for a moment?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In your dreams! We're holding onto this!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: So stingy! Don't you know that I was the one who found the relics used by Sanhaj to open up his passages? I didn't kick up a fuss when they fell neatly into your hands, did I?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: You could learn a thing or two from someone with my magnanimity, Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... Paimon really wants to give this guy a good slap, but she doesn't want to accidentally end up hitting Citlali...

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: <color=#E1A4D0>Slap away. It won't hurt me.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Well, excuse me! I'm just a clerk — I've never hurt a soul. Is the crime of my wanting to come here and have a look around really deserving of such unjust violence?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: <color=#E1A4D0>He's not wrong... Papar wasn't hurt — I checked.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we were tricked! He hurt our feelings!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: I fully sympathize, Paimon, I do. But as you can see, I now have an old hag bouncing around in my brain.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: If that isn't punishment enough, then I'm afraid you might as well just kill me!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds good to me!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: #Et tu, {NICKNAME}? I thought a hero of your acclaim would say something in my defense, but here you stand, poised to strike me down with a cold blade!

choices.text: As long as it doesn't affect Citlali.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: <color=#E1A4D0>Well said.</color>

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: ...Let's stop talking about this. Present circumstances dictate that we should be trying to work together.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Remind Paimon, since when were we ever a "team"?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: This is the Mare Jivari, it's not like we have a choice! We've been in the same boat since the very start, and our enemies are the metaphorical sea and its storms.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: You all saw that scary creature just now, right? Although it was also my first time laying eyes on it, my wealth of wisdom tells me that it was likely Bakunawa's permeation...

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: If we don't deal with it, it'll eat us. If it eats us, it'll get stronger. If it gets stronger, it'll escape into Natlan and continue eating until there's nothing left.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bakunawa... That's the monster that Tenoch and the six heroes of ancient Natlan fought against... Wait, didn't they defeat it?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Ha! You wish. The worst part about the beast is that it has even stronger immortality than the rest of "Gold"'s creations. Its "permeation" is no simple humus or chalk...

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: The power contained within it was something that even "Gold" and the Abyss Order couldn't harness. A power that can corrupt even the passage of time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Venti also mentioned something about the contamination of time in the Mare Jivari... So this monster's the one behind it?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: <color=#E1A4D0>We did encounter our fair share of obstacles on the way here, maybe because people were trying to keep Bakunawa from escaping through the seals... Is that why the Mare disappeared...?</color>

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, we didn't break the seals by coming here, did we!?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Hmm... Let's just assume that we're in a different time from Bakunawa for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—Then how are we gonna get home!?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Our path is clear, Paimon. If the problem lies in Bakunawa's permeation, then in the name of the Abyss Order, we must slay the beast!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Why are you acting like a good guy all of a sudden? Pick a side and stick to it, will you?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Perhaps if you were more well-read, you would understand. The "New Tide Anthology" states that "principles" are defined by their "flexibility." Flexible principles, are to be in principle, flexible.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: In any case, the time has come for us to fight!

choices.text: Fine, I'll put in a good word for you.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: That's better. Now we're acting more like a team.

dialogues.speaker: Pucli
dialogues.text: If Papar isn't in "Tenoyollotzin," then where IS Papar?!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About "Bakunawa"...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Of all the Abyssal monsters that attacked Natlan five hundred years ago, Bakunawa was the most terrifying. It was said to have devoured entire villages of tribespeople and could not be killed...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Even when it was beheaded or had its body chopped into pieces, the remains would somehow continue to grow, seeking each other out and eventually... forming a new, revitalized Bakunawa.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What in the... How was it finally defeated, then?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Through Tenoch's sacrifice. He let Sanhaj perform Phlogiston Engraving on his body in order to unleash the power of border spells. Then, Tenoch allowed himself to be eaten by the beast.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: With Tenoch's body as the ritual offering, Sanhaj summoned a miniature Night Kingdom inside Bakunawa's belly.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The clash between the powers of the Abyss, the Lord of the Night, and Tenoch's spirit in Bakunawa's body led to a violent explosion that shattered the monster into innumerable pieces.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yet even so, some believe it never truly died, and that its rebirth was merely suppressed by the chaotic energies unleashed in the blast.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: If the right conditions are met, the beast's remains could potentially still grow into a new Bakunawa once more...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did we get rid of it? Woohoo, we're awesome! That's the biggest bad guy we've ever taken down!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Hehe... Judging by the potency of the energy we just dealt with, that may only have been one piece of Bakunawa's body.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: But even if it's only one of many, I'm sure it will've left something useful behind... Let's see...

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: <color=#E1A4D0>Stop right there.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You heard her, Enjou! Stay put!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: What's this now? Are your companions naught but arrows in your quiver, fit only to be strung, shot, and then abandoned?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, remind me, who was it who dealt the crucial blow to Bakunawa just now, hmm? Is this how you treat the backbone of your team?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: B—B—Backbone!? Keep dreaming...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What exactly are you after?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: All that is unknown etches itself into the desires of my soul.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: The corpse of Bakunawa may be laden with ancient treasures it once devoured, surely such artifacts would be priceless...

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: #<color=#E1A4D0>Try harder. You've been hunting for clues about the Mare Jivari since {NICKNAME}'s arrival in Natlan. There's no way your end goal is something so vague.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can't lie your way outta this one, Enjou! What secrets are you hiding? We're not giving up until you spill the beans!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Lie? Why, I'm not lying at all... But since you insist, I'll grace you with a story.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Many years ago, there existed a kingdom in a broken land. The king was wise and powerful — he loved his people and was beloved by them.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Later, when a powerful enemy attacked the kingdom, the king sacrificed his life to save it. Upon his death, his most steadfast follower succeeded him.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Yet evil still lurked in the shadows, its creeping corruption poisoning the new king. Once more, the kingdom was plunged into torment...

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Civil war broke out across the kingdom, splitting it into factions. The wicked king was slain, and his people were exiled from the land.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: These exiles split into two different groups. One chose to accept their exile, and abandoned their homeland forever.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: The other group refused to leave, until they were allowed to settle down elsewhere, albeit in the most barren and remote part of their nation.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: They lived in neglect for millennia until darkness returned once more. The kingdom was still divided, and these exiles were the first to raise their weapons.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Although they were destitute, not a single one of them retreated or fled. With the same stubborn spirit that bade them never abandon their homeland all those years ago, they fought and died until, at last, only one remained.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're not going to tell us that survivor... was you!?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Hmph. It seems like eating too many Slimes really can make someone a dullard...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon was just guessing! Where'd you get off being so mean!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: ...In any case, that man's name was Tenoch, and the lost settlement was known as Tenochtzitoc.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Its people were warriors who wielded the power of Anemo. Some people named the place where their bones were buried the "Windless Land."

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: While their brothers and sisters — who 500 years before departed from their homeland — headed to the true land of wind. There, they were known by another name, the "Muratans"... However, that's a story for another day.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Does this mean... you're one of these Muratan people?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: R—Really? Is he lying again, Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: #Don't shout so loudly, or you'll kill off all dear {NICKNAME}'s brain cells. As for your beloved Granny Itztli... She can no longer respond to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What did you do to her!?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Nothing of consequence, I merely drove her away. Stories all have a purpose, and I thank you for taking the time to listen to this one, as it has allowed me to familiarize myself with some of Bakunawa's powers.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: From now on, that old hag shan't be bothering us anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sneaky, lying, scheming, evil Abyssal rat!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Flexible principles, Paimon, flexible principles. See, that is where your problem lies. You never listen to what others have to say.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who exactly are you, and what's your objective?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, I have seen the glory of Vindagnyr perish, buried beneath the snow. I have witnessed the Sunchildren dancing in their Whitenight, and beheld the magnificence of Gurabad, submerged in the sea of sand...

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: I have touched the vessels of flesh and blood in the Moshiri Ceremonial Site, the broken colossi of Remuria, and brushed my fingers across the soiled colors of the murals in the Vucub Caquix Tower...

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: I know how Mondstadt's old aristocracy was overthrown, how the people of Liyue began the great migration of the Guili Assembly, and how the loyalists of Orobaxi fought against the disciples of Narukami.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: I even know how the people of Tenochtzitoc perished in battle, and how the Muratans left for a distant land...

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: But none of these places in my memory belong to me. They are like shooting stars, merely flitting across my sky with a spark, then fading away into nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon. I serve the Abyss Order, but the Order is not my home. What about you two? Where is your home?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: ...Ah, so you cannot answer that. Or perhaps you do not wish to answer?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Very well. I will be heading deeper to continue my investigation. Maybe we shall never see each other again.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: #But know this, {NICKNAME}. Without the power of Bakunawa, you will never be able to enter the true Mare Jivari. Allow me to leave you a final parting gift.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What... is this?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: This is the flower that blooms in flames. Until the day that the fires turn me into ashes, you shall see the glowing embers of this flower shining through the dark smoke.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: <color=#E1A4D0>Hey, you're called Enjou, right? If you find any secrets, remember to come back and tell us... Or at least give us your name. Your real name.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Granny Itztli...? Why, I swore I had driven you away.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: <color=#E1A4D0>Me, by the likes of you? Pff! Granny just wanted to see if you had any other parlor tricks up your sleeves.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Hehe, so that's how it is. Granny will always be Granny... I apologize for my hubris. If that day does come, I promise I will.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: And with that, I bid you farewell, you monuments on my journey. Until we meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: If there truly is a homeland I have forgotten, could it be within this realm of smoldering, shattered time?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You're back! Are you both alright?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're okay.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's a relief. I couldn't see what Enjou was up to... Tch, unreadable to the very end.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Now that I think about it, when Enjou was hiding inside "Tenoyollotzin," I don't think he was able to enter this place.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But he knew you would come, and he planned to use you. Naturally, he was certain you would somehow find a way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But he didn't bet on Citlali showing up, which threw a wrench into his works!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We always knew this guy wasn't like the other Abyss Order goons...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon never thought he'd have so many secrets, and asking him for answers only left us with more questions! Just like this place...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'll check with Mavuika. I have a feeling she'll know something about this place.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I let Citlalin scout the area, and it found a stone tablet behind the temple. It just so happens there were some names written on it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Names?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Some of them have been eroded beyond recognition, while others are barely legible. They are the names of the former Pyro Archons.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I have an inkling this place may have been put together by the Pyro Archons five hundred years ago. They must have made it to deal with, or at least temporarily contain, Bakunawa.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But the exact methods they used are still a mystery... Anyway, I'd appreciate it if you don't tell anyone else about this. For now, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then... Can we keep looking around this place?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Of course, but you shouldn't stray too deep. Especially you, {NICKNAME}. Got that?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The spirit trace I left on Enjou seems to have been consumed by a strange power... Whatever's wrong with the Mare Jivari, we're definitely not equipped to handle it right now.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I need some time to look into all this. Of course, if I learn anything useful, you'll be the first to hear about it.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Is there anything else you'd like to know?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's the employee who was acting up earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Papar? He's fine. Enjou told me that he previously disguised himself as a tourist and adopted the name "Hayne." He then approached Papar, and the two of them really hit it off.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: In the end, Enjou fed Papar enough Aphimead to knock out a Tatankasaurus. He's probably still snoozing it off in a corner of Tete Isle somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Classic Enjou.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I should really be heading home — for a senior citizen like myself, this excursion has been a headache and a half...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, Citlali.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I didn't ask for anyone's thanks...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ahem! But, well, if you really want to express your gratitude, remember to come and visit your Granny more often, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Mare Jivari...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Enjou failed to uncover the mystery of the Mare Jivari's disappearance, which is good news for us.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But his hypothesis... is a little hard to believe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like we've reached the end... What's this? It looks familiar.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's a mystic arts implement from the Masters of the Night-Wind. But how did it end up here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks we've seen those around... Hmm, it can transport us to other places, right?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's correct. Our tribespeople use them to transport themselves to the Chamber of Weaving or the Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land. But this one doesn't lead to either of those places, evidently...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where do you think it goes?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The only people who would know where it leads are the spellcaster and anyone else who's used it. Unfortunately, it looks like this implement's too old to work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Too old?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So old that its spirit has long since dissipated... I doubt that Enjou brat could've found a way around this either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there any way to... y'know, replenish its spirit? To make it work again?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: There is a way — but every spellcaster is like a different lock, each needing their own key to open. I'll have to figure out the structure of this implement's "lock" before we can get it up and running again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just like that? Wow, Citlali, you're amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Obviously! Look up my name in the "Night-Wind Dictionary", and you'll find three words: the — real — shadeal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Shadeal"? That doesn't sound like a real word to Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Of course it is! It means a "shaman who's the (real) deal."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about the definition of "Ororon"?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: "A cultisham."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A shaman whose skills you cultivated?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: No, a shaman who cultivates vegetables!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhm... you didn't write this dictionary yourself, did you, Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's enough jokes for now. Just give me a moment to look at... Wait. Who goes there!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We were followed!? Whoever you are, come out with your hands up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's just some Asha... You scared Paimon half to death, she thought it was that awful Enjou guy!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Odd... Why are there Asha following us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe they like us? Pucli told us that Asha are the "benevolent souls" of the Mare Jivari. They're friendly sorts, hehe!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You mean how "benevolent soul" is one of the ways to interpret the word "Asha"? I've heard that said before, but it doesn't solve the mystery of why they followed us all the way here.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hold on, I think I've got it. Maybe they're not just being friendly...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What else could it be?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Maybe they're after something we're carrying. If they're the "benevolent souls" of the Mare Jivari, it'd make perfect sense for them to be drawn to it. Do the honors, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Take out Sanhaj's relic)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sanhaj's relic! Oh wow, the Asha are really happy... They must've seen Citlali take it out just now, and followed us ever since.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: A reunion after all these years...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wah! What are they doing?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The implement! It's active again! But how...?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Aha... It seems the Asha were the key we needed for the lock...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: We might not know who left this implement behind, but the place it points to must have something to do with the Mare Jivari...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Should we go and take a look around?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Only if you're both ready. We can't wait too long — that brat from the Abyss Order is going to catch up to us sooner or later.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the "secret cave"...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It seems like Enjou memorized our map after he snuck a peek at it. This is his redrawing of it.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Judging by the markings, he must have found his destination.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bleh! So why didn't he do anything? He just wasted his time out here putting on a show!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Given the cunning he's displayed so far, I doubt he did so without purpose. His act must have been necessary for him to break through certain obstacles.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: If I'm not mistaken, that man's name is "Kokuchuu." I've run into him once before, but unfortunately, he got away.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I looked into him a little more and found out he once escaped from Kinich while using a different name, "Sanka"... It turns out he's one slippery rat.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Kinich even told me you've crossed paths with him before...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've crossed paths... Wait, there's no way... I—It's Enjou!?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: "Enjou"? Is that his real name...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It could be another alias.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whatever he's called, he's a clerk who works for the Abyss Order. He's great at lying and great at slipping away... Are you here to catch him, Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So he's an Abyss Order goon. Hmph! On my life, I am NOT letting him get away this time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali, you're starting to get a little scary... What did he do to you?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That Enjou... He once tried to coax Leyla into doing something dangerous, but thankfully, Ororon stepped in before it was too late.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Some good came out of it in the end. After putting his soul in danger, Leyla gained an affinity for clairvoyance... though it's not like helping him was in Enjou's playbook. Enjou just wanted to sacrifice Leyla to get information about the Mare Jivari.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Urgh... It all happened so suddenly that Enjou ended up giving us the slip. This was all I got from him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's a relic that was owned by the legendary Border Master, Sanhaj Kompore. I used it to divine the location of the Mare Jivari.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's a map. Here, have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Is this all we need to find the Mare Jivari!?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm not making any promises, but it's a start. Last time, Enjou took advantage of us helping Leyla, he hid in the shadows so he could peek at this very map.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... So that's why he came all the way here?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It appears so...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (That rat! He should know you don't mess with an old lady's pride, yet that lousy fiend took me for a fool! Just you wait, Granny Itztli's going to make you regret the day you were born!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm... Hey, Citlali! Is everything okay? You're making a really scary face...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ahem! Even though he got away from me last time, I made sure to leave a mark on him. That way, I can track the rat no matter what hole he decides to crawl into. As long as he's nearby, I'll be able to sense him.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I had a vague sense of where he was from the moment I set foot in the resort. I never expected to bump into you two while tracking him, though.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you're saying he's nearby?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yes. Unfortunately, the mark only gives me a rough guide to where he is... otherwise, I'd have caught him already.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #We should work together, {NICKNAME}. I get a sense that Enjou might have something to do with that employee's strange behavior.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awesome! With Citlali here, there's nothing to fear!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
